sections.name: PARTIES AND REASONS FOR JURISDICTION.
sentences: Plaintiff, Vivian Garza, is an adult individual residing at the above address.

Defendant, NOSCO, Inc. (hereinafter “NOSCO”) is a corporation, organized and existing under the laws of the Illinois, registered to do business in Pennsylvania and with a principal place of business at the 1504 Grundy Lane, Bristol, PA 19007.

sections.name: Operative Facts.
sentences: On or about July 22, 2019, Ms. Garza was an employee hired through Defendant, Randstad, to work at the Defendant, NOSCO’s, plant as a Catcher on the Glue Line.
Ms. Garza was qualified for her position and performed all her duties for Defendants without complaint or issue.
In fact, on or about September 16, 2019, Ms. Garza’s supervisor, Randy, told her that NOSCO desired to promote her to a Top-Quality Inspector.
On or about September 23, 2019, Ms. Garza learned that she was pregnant.
On or about September 23, 2019, Ms. Garza informed Randy that she was pregnant.
Ms. Garza was told by Randy that this was not a problem and she proactively attempted to obtain a doctor’s note confirming that she could work around the chemicals in the facility.
On or about September 24, 2019, Ms. Garza reported to work, but was experiencing bad morning sickness.
Ms. Garza advised Randy that she was feeling ill and he sent her home.
During this interaction, Randy also discussed the possibility of moving Ms. Garza to second shift, along with a promotion.

Later that day, Ms. Garza scheduled a doctor’s appointment to verify that it was permissible to work around the chemicals in the plant and to obtain a doctor’s note to that effect to provide to NOSCO.
That same day, Ms. Garza received communication from Randstad that stating that her employment with NOSCO had been terminated due to performance.

Ms. Garza requested documentation from Randstad as to why her contract was terminated and she was advised by Randstad that, “they couldn’t give her that.” On or about October 1, 2019, Ms. Garza filed a complaint of pregnancy discrimination with NOSCO’s Human Resources Department.
On or about October 14, 2019, Ms. Garza was contacted by Kerry Lennon of Randstad’s Human Resources concerning her complaint.
On November 5, 2019, Ms. Garza provided an email to Ms. Lennon outlining the basis of her complaint.
On November 26, 2019, Ms. Lennon emailed Ms. Garza that she would continue to look into her concerns and provide an update as soon as possible.
On March 6, 2020, Ms. Joanie Orzo from Randstad’s Human Resources called Ms. Garza to discuss her complaint.
During the call Ms. Orzo advised Ms. Garza that NOSCO had provided her verbal counseling in December of 2019 about her poor performance.
After the call, Ms. Garza wrote Ms. Orzo an email stating that she could not have received verbal counseling from NOSCO in December of 2019, because she was terminated in September of 2019.
Ms. Garza also advised Ms. Orzo that she was never contacted by Randstad about another assignment.
Ms. Orzo responded that Ms. Garza’s employment with Randstad was not terminated, only her assignment with NOSCO.
Despite Ms. Orzo telling Ms. Garza this, Ms. Garza never received another assignment from Randstad, thereby terminating her employment.
Upon information and belief, NOSCO terminated Ms. Garza’s employment because she was pregnant.
Upon information and belief, Randstad terminated Ms. Garza’s employment because she was pregnant and engaged in protected activity by complaining about pregnancy discrimination.

As a direct and proximate result of Defendants’ conduct in terminating Ms. Garza’s employment, Ms. Garza has sustained great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, as well emotional distress, humiliation, pain and suffering and other damages as set forth below.
III. Causes of Action.

sections.name: CAUSES OF ACTION.
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-33 as if fully set forth at length herein.
Defendants took adverse action against Plaintiff by terminating her employment.

sections.name: COUNT I – EMPLOYMENT DISCRIMINATION (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000e-2(a)).
sentences: Plaintiff’s status as a pregnant and childbearing woman places her in a protected class.
Plaintiff’s membership in a protected class was a motivating factor in Defendants’ decisions to terminate her employment.

sections.name: COUNT II – RETALIATION (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000e-3(a)).
sentences: Defendant Randstad took adverse action against Plaintiff by terminating her employment.
As set forth above, Plaintiff’s participation in protected activity was a motivating factor in Defendant Randstad’s decision to terminate her employment.

sections.name: COUNT III—PREGNANCY DISCRIMINATION ACT (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000(e)(k) et seq).
sentences: At all times material hereto, and pursuant to the Pregnancy Discrimination Act an employer may not discriminate against an employee on the basis of pregnancy, childbirth or other medical conditions.

Defendants’ conduct in terminating and Plaintiff’s employment is an adverse action, and was taken as a result of her pregnancy and, as such, constitutes a violation of the Pregnancy Discrimination Act, 42 U.S.C. §2000(e)(k), et seq.

sections.name: PRAYER FOR RELIEF.
sentences: Compensatory damages, including but not limited to: back pay, front pay, past lost wages, future lost wages. Lost pay increases, lost pay incentives, lost opportunity, lost benefits, lost future earning capacity, injury to reputation, mental and emotional distress, pain and suffering.
Punitive damages;.
Attorneys’ fees and costs of suit;.
Interest, delay damages; and,.
Any other further relief this Court deems just proper and equitable.

sections.name: COUNT I – EMPLOYMENT DISCRIMINATION
sentences: (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000e-2(a)) (Plaintiff v. Defendants) Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-33 as if fully set forth at length herein.
Defendants took adverse action against Plaintiff by terminating her employment.
Plaintiff’s status as a pregnant and childbearing woman places her in a protected class.
Plaintiff’s membership in a protected class was a motivating factor in Defendants’ decisions to terminate her employment.
As such, Defendants’ decisions to terminate Plaintiff’s employment is an unlawful employment practice, under 42. U.S.C. § 2000e-2(a).

As a proximate result of Defendants’ conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
As a result of the conduct of Defendants’ owners/management, Plaintiff hereby demands punitive damages.
Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. §2000e-2(a), et seq Plaintiff demands attorneys’ fees and court costs.

sections.name: COUNT II – RETALIATION
sentences: (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000e-3(a)) (Plaintiff v. Defendant Randstad) Plaintiff incorporates paragraph 1-41 as if fully set forth at length herein.

At set forth above, Plaintiff complained about discrimination by Defendant NOSCO and as such, Plaintiff was engaged in protected activity under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act. Defendant Randstad took adverse action against Plaintiff by terminating her employment.
As set forth above, Plaintiff’s participation in protected activity was a motivating factor in Defendant Randstad’s decision to terminate her employment.
As such, Defendant Randstad's decision to terminate Plaintiff’s employment is a retaliatory action prohibited by the Civil Rights Act of 1964, §704(a).

As a proximate result of Defendant Randstad's conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
As a result of the conduct of Defendant Randstad, Plaintiff hereby demands punitive damages.
Pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, §704(a), 42 U.S.C. §2000e- 3(a), et seq., Plaintiff demands attorneys’ fees and court costs.

sections.name: COUNT III—PREGNANCY DISCRIMINATION ACT
sentences: (42 U.S.C.A. § 2000(e)(k) et seq) (Plaintiff v. Defendants) Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-49 as if fully set forth at length herein.
At all times material hereto, and pursuant to the Pregnancy Discrimination Act an employer may not discriminate against an employee on the basis of pregnancy, childbirth or other medical conditions.
At all times material hereto, Plaintiff was pregnant and subject to the aforementioned adverse actions, as described above.

Defendants’ conduct in terminating and Plaintiff’s employment is an adverse action, and was taken as a result of her pregnancy and, as such, constitutes a violation of the Pregnancy Discrimination Act, 42 U.S.C. §2000(e)(k), et seq. As a proximate result of Defendants’ conduct, Plaintiff sustained significant damages, including but not limited to: great economic loss, future lost earning capacity, lost opportunity, loss of future wages, loss of front pay, loss of back pay, as well as emotional distress, mental anguish, humiliation, pain and suffering, consequential damages and Plaintiff has also sustained work loss, loss of opportunity, and a permanent diminution of her earning power and capacity and a claim is made therefore.
As a result of the conduct of Defendants’ owners/management, Plaintiff hereby demands punitive damages.
Pursuant to the Pregnancy Discrimination Act, Plaintiff demands attorneys’ fees and court costs.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff, Vivian Garza, seeks damages and legal and equitable relief in connection with Defendants’ improper conduct, and specifically prays that the Court grant the following relief to Plaintiff by: Compensatory damages, including but not limited to: back pay, front pay, past lost wages, future lost wages.

Lost pay increases, lost pay incentives, lost opportunity, lost benefits, lost future earning capacity, injury to reputation, mental and emotional distress, pain and suffering Punitive damages; Attorneys’ fees and costs of suit; Interest, delay damages; and, Any other further relief this Court deems just proper and equitable.
